title: Late Breaking Results: Fine-Tuning LLMs for Test Stimuli Generation
problem: LLMs fine-tuned for hardware test stimuli generation often produce inconsistent or incorrect outputs; existing prompt engineering and feedback mechanisms do not effectively improve domain-specific performance in test generation.
motivation: Automated test stimulus generation with high code coverage and syntax correctness is essential for reducing hardware verification time; LLMs show promise but need better domain-specific adaptation.
method: Two-stage fine-tuning framework: first generates a table-shaped test stimuli dataset to ensure LLM output consistency, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to provide corrective feedback on generated outputs. The approach trains LLMs on domain-specific data with RL signals tuned for test coverage and correctness.
key_novelty: Domain-specific LLM fine-tuning via table-shaped dataset generation followed by RL feedback, specifically targeting test stimuli generation performance.
contributions: Dataset generation strategy producing table-shaped test stimuli for consistent LLM outputs
Two-stage fine-tuning with RL feedback for domain-specific test generation
Improved syntax correctness and code coverage outperforming commercial models

metrics.other: improved syntax correctness and code coverage vs. commercial models
